material.notes: ROUND 77 (m, compared to Flutter Tooltip, docs/ui/looks/flutter-compare-m.md): plain tooltip 24 high on inverse-surface 322f35 against Flutter's 32 high grey 707070 (M3 24, kept); the rich tooltip's left edge column is still half a pixel off Material Web (round 33, not touched), and Flutter has no rich tooltip. Stays review. | ROUND 37 (restated): Android text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model (93 to 96 percent of ink exact; a second mode, AndroidSkia, exists beside ChromeWin) and the references are Chrome for Testing on Windows with greyscale text, not Linux Chromium. Older notes below that describe another text model are history. | ROUND 33 (still review, one defect left): the plain tooltip is flat 0 off in light and dark; the rich tooltip is flat 0 off with 6 glyph px (147 after the baseline fix, 17 before): its text sat one pixel high and moved with the Blink metrics (plate padding 12 above, 14 before the action row). The rich plate is placed BelowEnd against the anchor and its fractional width puts the left edge half a pixel into a column (ring 218 px light, 112 dark: two columns by 110 rows); snapping the placed rectangle moved the card a whole pixel and was reverted. | ROUND 33 method: scripts/material/cmp.py (flat px off, ring px over 12 levels, rim px over 40, shadow) on the committed 1x sheets, light and dark, plus a text ink comparison (ink = reference pixels that differ from its -notext render; rms of the per-pixel difference); scripts/looks_scale_check.py material:<sheet> passes at 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0 (all runs within a device pixel). Round 33 changes sit behind the Android profile: Blink line metrics (ascent up, descent down to whole pixels, floored half leading), svg icons on whole device pixels, quarter pixel glyph positions with a 7 % sideways spread and a luminance keyed power on text coverage, Skia's corner polygons and a 1.2 power on path coverage. Sampled Linux, Windows, Cupertino and Neper sheets re-rendered stay byte for byte. ROUND 37: the text edge percentages and 'not pixel equal' findings above predate the round 35 DirectWrite model and are superseded by the last gap.
gaps: Rich tooltip left edge column: the plate's width is fractional where Chrome's box is whole pixels (218 ring px light, 112 dark).

Text follows the Chrome-on-Windows DirectWrite model of android-text.md (hinted outline, six by five samples, ClearType boxes averaged to grey, Skia's pre-blend table), which is how the Chrome for Testing on Windows references are drawn: 93 to 96 % of text ink pixels are exact (every channel within 2 levels) on the Material sheets, the rest are anti-aliasing edges of single glyphs. A second mode, AndroidSkia (a device's Skia over FreeType), exists next to it for Android devices; no device capture exists to measure it against.
